To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

nutrient enrichment of lakes with contrasting food web structure and planktonic community structure resulted in a trophic cascade in which nutrient‐induced increases in primary productivity and phytoplankton biomass were attenuated by herbivorous zooplplankton.
(a) the food web structure of a lake can have large effects on its productivity, and (b) the productivity of a lake is not necessarily limited by the availability of inorganic nutrients.

(1) the food web of West Long Lake is a trophic cascade that is driven by the piscivore-dominated food web of its watershed and that (2) the food web in Peter Lake is an alternative state that is driven by a planktivore-dominated food web in its watershed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of nutrient enrichment on lake food webs, and how these food web changes in turn influence the productivity of the lakes.
the role that nutrients and trophic cascades play in determining lake productivity and with the role of lake productivity in regulating CO2 fluxes from lakes to the atmosphere.
how nutrient loading and fish predation interact to control the structure and function of aquatic ecosystems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the food web structure in the four study lakes had no detectable effects on the rates of nutrient uptake, primary productivity or CO2 exchange with atmosphere.
the trophic cascade in the lakes studied here did not affect the magnitude of the response to nutrient addition, but that the cascade did affect the form of the response to enrichment.

nutrient additions to lakes with planktivorous fish stocks increase lake primary production, and that this increase can be attributed to increased phytoplankton biomass, and not to increased nutrient use efficiency or to increased phytoplanker growth rates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the food‐web manipulation had a major effect on nutrient limitation, which in turn affected lake productivity.
the food web and nutrient interactions that we have examined are important determinants of lake ecosystem function.
nutrient enrichment increased the productivity of the pelagic food web in all lakes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the food‐web structure of lakes, as modified by fish, is an important control on the responses of lake productivity to nutrient enrichment.
the food web and the stoichiometric composition of the organisms in the food web are important factors that determine the responses of lakes to nutrient enrichment.
the food‐web structure of a lake has a strong impact on the way in which nutrients affect the lake's productivity.
